preserved_objections.basis: The proposed mechanism relies on pH-responsive microcapsules releasing ion migration inhibitors, but the evidence bundle contains no studies demonstrating pH-triggered release of ion-blocking compounds in photovoltaic encapsulation materials, and no evidence that pH changes precede sodium ion migration in crystalline silicon modules.

The candidate fails to address boundary conditions of high-voltage string operation where multiple modules experience different thermal and electrical stresses simultaneously, potentially causing inconsistent microcapsule activation and creating new failure points in the string.
The evidence bundle references organic solar cells and perovskite materials, not crystalline silicon modules, contradicting the fundamental technology claimed in the problem statement.

The candidate provides no quantitative comparison against baseline degradation rates of existing modules, making the predicted 0.1% annual degradation an unsubstantiated claim that may not improve upon current commercial modules.

The proposed nanosensor network for molecular-level degradation detection does not exist in the current state of photovoltaic technology and would require breakthroughs in nanomanufacturing, power consumption, and data processing that are not supported by the evidence.

The testable prediction using accelerated aging tests fails to define how molecular-level degradation will be measured or correlated with voltage imbalances, making it impossible to validate whether the microcapsules are actually preventing degradation or merely delaying its detection.
